north_star: A player should understand the coaching thesis with the sound off in one replay, and the captions should sound like a coach talking over the shoulder—not a data dashboard.

semantic_encoding.actual: solid high-contrast geometry anchored to measured video objects
semantic_encoding.self_best: translucent ghost or corridor aligned by event; never imply universal ideal
semantic_encoding.target_window: bounded corridor/zone, not a single forced pose
semantic_encoding.causal_link: animated time-directed connector from earlier event to later effect
semantic_encoding.strength: positive badge + repeatability trace; never color-only
semantic_encoding.suppressed_detail: available in tap/coach mode, not player replay

player_mode_limits.rule: If an overlay requires a legend to understand, it is probably coach-mode.

beats.action: Play at near full speed into the causal window; dim irrelevant region slightly.
beats.caption: Watch the setup before the hit.

beats.action: Freeze/slow at earliest divergence. Draw only the evidence that proves the cause.
beats.caption: This is where it starts.

beats.action: Animate the causal connector forward in time while video advances toward contact.
beats.caption: Now the next option gets smaller.

beats.action: At contact show actual vs self-best consequence, then immediately remove auxiliary overlays.
beats.caption: Here is the contact consequence.

beats.action: Replay the same window with one target corridor and one short cue.
beats.caption: Give yourself the better window.

beats.action: Clean replay with only a tiny cue tag; no skeleton.
beats.caption: Now watch it with the cue.

beats.action: Synchronize current and best rep to bounce/contact.
Overlay only until the first meaningful divergence; stop ghosting after the comparison stops being valid.
Show the difference as a corridor or motion trail, not a complete pro skeleton.
Show resulting contact/outcome difference.
End on one player-owned cue: 'This is already in your game.'
Show a compact timeline: bounce | turn complete | forward swing | contact.
Highlight the shrinking or expanding time reserve against player's successful band.
As timeline cursor moves, highlight only the matching movement in video.
Replace milliseconds with a feel cue for player mode; keep numbers for advanced/coach.
Show 2-3 reps where pattern works.
Show 2-3 matched reps from the context that exposes the issue.
Highlight one changing variable and the earliest movement response.
State the conditional coaching rule: 'On deep balls, keep adjusting longer.'
Rapidly show three successful reps with the same stable feature.
Mark the feature 'KEEP THIS' while introducing the separate correction.

camera_alignment_rules: Use ghost overlays only when body/court alignment error is acceptable.
If camera/player scale differs too much, use synchronized side-by-side rather than silhouette overlay.
If court calibration is unavailable, keep comparisons body-normalized and avoid world-coordinate arrows.
accessibility: Every color distinction also uses label/shape/line style.
Provide text alternative describing each visual beat.
Never flash high-frequency overlays around contact.
narration_rule: Narration may explain the thesis, but the geometry must still make sense without narration.

caption_language_contract.sequence_rule: Each beat must advance the coaching sentence; do not restate the same diagnosis in different words.
caption_language_contract.player_vocabulary: Use the stroke_coach_lexicon for the active stroke.
caption_language_contract.numbers: No raw measurements in captions unless the number itself is the teaching point.
caption_language_contract.confidence: If a visual is estimated, mark it visually; do not clutter the caption with model-confidence language.

narration_contract.style: short spoken coach phrases synchronized to the visual beat
narration_contract.rule: Narration must not introduce a new diagnosis that the current beat does not show.
narration_contract.clean_replay_end: Always end the primary correction story with a clean or nearly clean replay and the single active cue.
